description.en: The Andean condor (Vultur gryphus) is a massive South American Cathartid vulture and the largest flying bird in the world by combined measurement of weight and wingspan. Inhabiting the rugged terrain of the Andes mountains and adjacent Pacific coasts, this apex scavenger plays a critical ecological role in disease control by disposing of carrion. Characterized by a striking bald head, a distinctive white collar, and profound sexual dimorphism where males possess a prominent fleshy caruncle, the condor is a master of soaring flight, utilizing thermal updrafts to traverse hundreds of kilometers daily with minimal energy expenditure.
description.zh: 安第斯神鹫（Vultur gryphus），又名康多兀鹫，是南美洲一种体型巨大的美洲鹫科鸟类，也是世界上体重与翼展综合尺寸最大的现存飞禽。它们栖息于安第斯山脉的崎岖高地及毗邻的太平洋海岸，作为顶级食腐动物，通过清除动物尸体在控制疾病传播方面发挥着至关重要的生态作用。其形态特征包括裸露的头部、醒目的白色颈环，以及显著的雌雄异形现象（雄性头部具有肉冠）。安第斯神鹫是滑翔飞行的大师，能够巧妙利用上升热气流，以极低的能量消耗每天巡航数百公里。

anatomy.en: Andean condor is a member of Cathartidae within Cathartiformes. Species-level identification should combine several visible characters with location and the accepted scientific name Vultur gryphus.
anatomy.zh: 安第斯神鹫属于美洲鹫目美洲鹫科。物种级鉴定应结合多个可见特征、地点和接受学名Vultur gryphus。

ecology_and_behavior.en: This review classifies the species as scavenger. Feeding, social behavior and activity can vary with age, season and locality, so details are tied to the cited species account rather than generalized from one observation.
ecology_and_behavior.zh: 本次复核把该物种归为食腐性。取食、社会行为和活动会随年龄、季节与地点变化，因此细节应对应所引物种资料，不能从一次观察泛化。

habitat_and_distribution.en: The species is endemic to South America, distributed continuously along the Andes mountain range from Venezuela and Colombia in the north, through Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, and Chile, down to Tierra del Fuego in Argentina. They favor high-altitude alpine regions up to 5000 meters, characterized by open grasslands and alpine tundra, which facilitate the detection of carrion from the air. They also frequent coastal regions with strong sea breezes and desert cliffs that provide optimal nesting sites and reliable thermal updrafts.
habitat_and_distribution.zh: 该物种是南美洲的特有种，沿着安第斯山脉呈连续分布，北起委内瑞拉和哥伦比亚，途经厄瓜多尔、秘鲁、玻利维亚和智利，南至阿根廷的火地岛。它们偏好海拔高达5000米的高山地区，这些地区以开阔的草原和高山冻原为特征，便于从空中搜寻尸体。它们也经常出没于海风强劲的沿海地区和沙漠悬崖，这些地形为它们提供了理想的筑巢地点和可靠的上升热气流。

habitat.text_en: Endemic to the Andes mountains and adjacent Pacific coasts of South America, ranging from Colombia to Tierra del Fuego.
habitat.text_zh: 特产于南美洲安第斯山脉及毗邻的太平洋海岸，分布范围北起哥伦比亚，南至火地岛。

similar_species.en: Close relatives and regional look-alikes may share color or body shape. Confirm records with multiple visible characters, location and an exact taxon-linked source rather than a filename or single feature.

communication_and_senses.en: The species uses the sensory channels available to its class—vision, sound, chemical cues, touch or vibration—in combinations shaped by its habitat. The cited species account should be used before assigning a specific call or signal.
communication_and_senses.zh: 该物种会组合使用其类群具备的视觉、声音、化学信号、触觉或振动等感官通道，具体组合受生境塑造。指定某种叫声或信号前，应查阅所引物种资料。

seasonal_calendar.en: Breeding, movement, molt, dormancy or food use can shift with latitude, rainfall, temperature and resource pulses. A date from one population must not be presented as universal.
seasonal_calendar.zh: 繁殖、迁移、换羽、休眠或食物利用会随纬度、降雨、温度和资源脉冲变化。不能把某一种群的日期写成全球统一规律。

relationship_with_humans.en: Use, conflict, tourism and cultural relationships vary across the range. Safe observation avoids handling, feeding, playback, nest or den disturbance, and any approach that changes natural behavior.
relationship_with_humans.zh: 利用、冲突、旅游和文化关系因分布区而异。安全观察应避免触摸、投喂、播放叫声、干扰巢穴或洞穴，以及任何改变自然行为的接近。

evolution.en: Vultur gryphus is placed in Vultur, family Cathartidae, order Cathartiformes. This review follows the accepted species match cited in the taxonomy source.
evolution.zh: Vultur gryphus归入神鹫属、美洲鹫科、美洲鹫目。本次复核遵循分类来源所引的接受种匹配。

field_signs.en: Tracks, calls, nests, feeding marks, molts or other indirect signs may narrow an identification but usually cannot confirm a species alone. Fresh sign near a dangerous or sensitive animal requires distance.
field_signs.zh: 足迹、叫声、巢、取食痕迹、蜕皮或其他间接线索可缩小鉴定范围，但通常不能单独确认物种。危险或敏感动物附近的新鲜痕迹意味着应保持距离。

text.en: Its accepted scientific name in this review is Vultur gryphus.
text.zh: 本次复核采用的接受学名是Vultur gryphus。
